question.prompt: How many \(4\)-digit positive integers (that is, integers between \(1000\) and \(9999,\) inclusive) having only even digits are divisible by \(5?\)

solutions.title: Count the digit choices
solutions.explanation:
Divisibility by \(5\) restricts the units digit, so start there. A multiple of \(5\) ends in \(0\) or \(5\); because every digit must be even, the units digit must be \(0\).

The thousands digit has \(4\) choices: \(2,4,6,8\). It cannot be zero because the number has four digits. Each of the hundreds and tens digits has \(5\) choices: \(0,2,4,6,8\). Digits may repeat.

For each thousands digit, every allowed hundreds digit can be combined with every allowed tens digit. Each resulting digit arrangement gives exactly one eligible integer, and every eligible integer arises this way. Thus the count is
\[
4\cdot5\cdot5\cdot1=\boxed{100},
\]
choice \(\textbf{B}\).
